source_text: ἐν καρδίᾳ τε καὶ σπλάγχνοις ἀποτεθειμένον λόγιον τῶν κρίσεων ὠνομάσθαι φαμέν. Ἐνδιαίτημα γὰρ ὥσπερ τοῦ ἐν ἡμῖν λογικοῦ καρδία καὶ σπλάγχνα. Ἐρήρεισται δὲ ὥσπερ καὶ ἐγκαταπέπηκται φυσικῶς τῷ ἐν ἡμῖν λογικῷ καὶ ἡ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ τῶν πρακτέων ὀρθή τε καὶ ἀδιάβλητος κρίσις, τοῦτ' ἔστιν, ἡ δικαιοκρισία, καὶ τὸ ἑκάστῳ πρέπον· ἢ γὰρ οὐχὶ λογική τις ἐν ἡμῖν τὰς τῶν πρακτέων ταλαντεύει φύσεις, καὶ ἀποκρίνει τῶν ἀμεινόνων τὸ ἄχαρί τε καὶ ἀλυσιτελές; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ πάνυ. {ΚΥΡ.} Κρίσιν δὲ ὀνομάζειν ἔθος τῇ θεοπνεύστῳ Γραφῇ τὴν ὀρθότητα καὶ δικαιοκρισίαν. Καὶ γοῦν ὁ θεσπέσιος ψάλλει Δαβίδ· «Μακάριοι οἱ φυλάσσοντες κρίσιν, καὶ ποιοῦντες δικαιοσύνην ἐν παντὶ καιρῷ.» Ἔφη δέ που πάλιν· «Καὶ τιμὴ βασιλέως, κρίσιν ἀγαπᾷν. Λαμπρὰ γὰρ ἡ βασιλέως τιμή τε καὶ δόξα, φιλοῦσα δικαιοσύνην. Λόγιον οὖν ἄρα κρίσεως τὸ καρδίᾳ καὶ στέρνοις ἐπεῤῥιμμένον, διὰ τὸ ὥσπερ ἐν τόπῳ κεῖσθαι τοῦ λογικοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἡ ὀρθότης ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ. Ἐν αὐτῷ δὲ τούτῳ λίθοι δυοκαίδεκα χρυσίῳ περισχετοὶ, γραφὴν ἔχοντες, τὰς φυλάς. Εἶεν δ' ἂν τύπος ἀνδρῶν ἁγίων, οἳ λαμπροί τέ εἰσι καὶ τίμιοι, καὶ οἷά τινες ἀπόλεκτοι λίθοι, μονονουχὶ καὶ εἰς νοῦν καὶ καρδίαν κείμενοι τοῦ Χριστοῦ· καὶ γάρ εἰσιν ἀληθῶς μνήμης ἄξιοι, διά γε τὸ ἐν ἀρετῇ διαφανὲς, καὶ τὸ ὡς ἐν ἁγιασμῷ τίμιον. Ἀποκρέμανται δὲ τοῦ λογίου τῶν κρίσεων καὶ κρωσσοὶ χρυσοῖ, παραδηλοῦντος, οἶμαι, τοῦ πράγματος, ὅτι τῆς τῶν ἁγίων πληθύος ὁ πολύς τε καὶ ἀναρίθμητος τῶν ἀνδραγαθημάτων ἐσμὸς μονονουχὶ καὶ ἀπηρτημένος ὁρᾶται. Καὶ γοῦν ὁ μακάριος Δαβὶδ καὶ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τὸν κόσμον ἐν κροσσωτοῖς εἶναί φησιν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πιθανὸς ὁ λόγος. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἀπὸ δέ γε τοῦ λογίου τῶν κρίσεων χρυσοῖς δακτύλοις ἐνειλημμένη ποικίλη τε καὶ εὔχρως ἀνέρπει σειρὰ, καθάπερ ἐλέγομεν, καὶ δι' ἀμφοῖν ἰοῦσα ταῖν ἀσπιδίσκαιν, ἐπ' αὐτὸ διήκει τῆς ἐπωμίδος τὸ ἄκρον, ἐφ' ᾗ τῆς ἀπογραφῆς αἱ λίθοι. Τί δ' ἂν εἴη καὶ τόδε, πῶς οὐκ ἄξιον ἰδεῖν; Δοκεῖ δὴ οὖν μοι παραδηλοῦν τὸ αἴνιγμα τοιουτονί τι πάλιν· Ὡς γὰρ οἱ λίθοι οἱ τίμιοι καὶ ἐν γνώσει τε καὶ ἐν μνήμῃ Χριστοῦ, πρὸς τὴν ἄνω τρέχοντες ἀπογραφὴν, τὸ χρῆμα κερδαίνουσι διὰ τῶν ὅπλων τῆς δικαιοσύνης τῶν δεξιῶν καὶ ἀριστερῶν· γράφει γὰρ ὧδε σαφῶς ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος. Καὶ μὴν καὶ ἑτέρωθί φησιν· «Ἐνδύσασθε τὴν πανοπλίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ.» Χρυσᾶ δὲ τὰ βασιλέως ὅπλα, χρυσαῖ δὲ ὁμοίως αἱ ἀσπιδίσκαι, καὶ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ πανοπλίαν αἰνιγματωδῶς ὑποφαίνουσαι. Ἐσόμεθα δὴ οὖν οὐχ ἑτέρως ἐν μνήμῃ τε καὶ ἀπογραφῇ Θεοῦ, μὴ οὐχὶ τῶν ὅπλων τῆς δικαιοσύνης ἁψάμενοι, καὶ δι' αὐτῶν ἰόντες πρακτικῶς. Τὸ δὲ δὴ τῆς ἐπωμίδος ἀνῆφθαι
pass_a_gloss: [continues] ...in heart and inward parts (σπλάγχνα) laid up (ἀποτεθειμένον) we say has been named oracle (λόγιον) of the judgments. For as a dwelling (ἐνδιαίτημα) of the rational (τὸ λογικόν) in us are heart and inward parts. And fixed (ἐρήρεισται) and as it were naturally (φυσικῶς) planted (ἐγκαταπέπηκται) in the rational in us is the right (ὀρθή) and blameless (ἀδιάβλητος) judgment (κρίσις) on each of the things to be done (πρακτέα), that is, just-judging (δικαιοκρισία), and what befits each; or is it not a rational [power] in us that weighs (ταλαντεύει) the natures of the things to be done and separates (ἀποκρίνει) from the better the graceless (ἄχαρι) and unprofitable (ἀλυσιτελές)? PALL.: Altogether. CYR.: Custom for God-breathed (θεόπνευστος) Scripture to name uprightness (ὀρθότης) and just-judging 'judgment'. Indeed the divine (θεσπέσιος) David sings: 'Blessed those keeping judgment and doing righteousness (δικαιοσύνη) at every time.' And again: 'And the honour (τιμή) of the king loves judgment.' For splendid (λαμπρά) is the king's honour and glory, loving righteousness. So the oracle of judgment is the thing thrown upon (ἐπερριμμένον) heart and breast, because it lies as in the place of the rational, in which is uprightness in righteousness. On it twelve stones enclosed with gold (περισχετοί), having writing (γραφή), the tribes. They would be a type of holy men, who are splendid and precious (τίμιοι), and as some choice (ἀπόλεκτοι) stones, all but lying in mind (νοῦς) and heart of Christ; for they are truly worthy of memory (μνήμη), through the translucence (διαφανές) in virtue (ἀρετή) and the preciousness in sanctification (ἁγιασμός). From the oracle hang golden tassels (κρωσσοί), the thing indicating, I think, that the great and countless swarm (ἑσμός) of noble deeds (ἀνδραγαθήματα) of the multitude (πληθύς) of the saints is seen as it were hung from it. Indeed blessed David says the adornment (κόσμος) of the Church is in fringes (κροσσωτοί). PALL.: Persuasive (πιθανός) the account. CYR.: From the oracle of judgments, gripped by golden rings/fingers (δάκτυλοι), a varied and well-coloured chain creeps up (ἀνέρπει), as we said, and going through both little shields reaches to the very top of the ephod, on which are the stones of the enrollment. What would this be, how not worth seeing? The riddle (αἴνιγμα) seems to me to indicate some such thing: that the precious stones, also in knowledge (γνῶσις) and memory of Christ, running toward the enrollment above, gain (κερδαίνουσι) the thing through the weapons (ὅπλα) of righteousness of the right and left; for so the divine Paul clearly writes. And elsewhere: 'Put on (ἐνδύσασθε) the full armour (πανοπλία) of God.' Golden are the king's weapons, golden likewise the little shields, indicating in riddling fashion (αἰνιγματωδῶς) the armour of God. We shall be then not otherwise in memory and enrollment of God, unless having taken hold (ἁψάμενοι) of the weapons of righteousness and going through them practically (πρακτικῶς). And the being fastened (ἀνῆφθαι) of the ephod... [breaks off; continues in section 9].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …in the heart and the inward parts has been named the oracle (logion) of judgments. For the heart and the inward parts are, so to speak, the dwelling place of the reason (logikon) within us. And firmly set, and as it were naturally fixed, in the reason within us is also right and blameless judgment about each thing to be done, that is, just judgment, and what befits each case. Or is it not some power of reason in us that weighs the nature of the things to be done, and separates what is unpleasant and unprofitable from what is better?

Cyril: It is the custom of the divinely inspired Scripture to call uprightness and just judgment ‘judgment’. So the divine David sings: ‘Blessed are those who keep judgment and do righteousness at all times’ (Psalm 106:3). And again he said somewhere: ‘And the honor of the king loves judgment’ (Psalm 99:4). For the honor and glory of a king is splendid when it loves righteousness. So, then, the piece laid upon the heart and breast is the oracle of judgment, because it lies, as it were, in the place of the reason, where uprightness in righteousness is found. On it are twelve stones set round with gold, bearing an inscription: the tribes. They would be a type of holy men, who are splendid and precious, like choice stones, lying, as it were, in the mind and heart of Christ. And they are truly worthy of remembrance, because of the brightness of their virtue and the worth of their sanctification. Golden fringes also hang from the oracle of judgments. The thing indicates, I think, that the great and countless host of noble deeds done by the multitude of the saints is seen, as it were, hanging from it. And indeed the blessed David says that the adornment of the Church is in fringes (Psalm 45:13).

Cyril: From the oracle of judgments, gripped by golden clasps, a many-colored and bright chain climbs upward, as we were saying, and passing through both little shields, it reaches the very top of the ephod, where the stones of the enrollment are. Is it not worth seeing what this, too, might mean? To me the riddle seems again to point to something like this: that the precious stones, which are in the knowledge and the memory of Christ, as they run toward the enrollment above, gain it through the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and for the left (2 Corinthians 6:7); for so the divine Paul plainly writes. And elsewhere he also says: ‘Put on the whole armor of God’ (Ephesians 6:11). A king’s weapons are golden, and golden likewise are the little shields, which hint, as in a riddle, at the whole armor of God. So we shall be in God’s memory and enrollment in no other way than by taking up the weapons of righteousness and making our way by them in action. And its being fastened to the ephod…
